strategy_description: Converting a one-shot elementwise kernel to a persistent grid-stride while-loop (1056 CTAs, each iterating ~3263 tiles) caused a catastrophic ~1230x slowdown: duration went from 2.12ms to 2.61 seconds. Although occupancy improved from 53% to 99.6% and compute throughput rose from 56.6% to 85%, the executed instruction count exploded from ~951M to ~1753T — a ~1.8 million-fold increase — indicating the while-loop was not bounded correctly or the Triton compiler unrolled/replicated the loop body pathologically. The persistent kernel pattern is fundamentally incompatible with this Triton kernel as implemented: the grid size in the launch remained 3,444,224 (unchanged from the original) rather than the intended 1,056, meaning every original CTA also ran the full grid-stride loop, multiplying work by ~3263x.
slow_pseudocode:
# Persistent grid-stride (BROKEN: grid not reduced to 1056)
pid = tl.program_id(0)  # still 3,444,224 PIDs launched
xoffset = pid * XBLOCK
stride = 1056 * XBLOCK   # hardcoded but grid was NOT changed
while xoffset < xnumel:  # each of 3.44M CTAs loops ~3263 times
    process_tile(xoffset)
    xoffset += stride
fast_pseudocode:
# Original one-shot (correct)
xoffset = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK  # 3,444,224 CTAs, each processes 1 tile
xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:]
process_tile(xindex)
tl.store(...)
applicable_when: NEVER: this specific pattern (persistent loop with hardcoded stride but unchanged grid size) always causes catastrophic regression by multiplying total work by grid_size/intended_persistent_grid_size.
do_not_apply_when: Any Triton elementwise kernel where the grid launch size is not simultaneously reduced to match the persistent CTA count. If the grid remains at the original size (3.44M) while the stride is set for 1056 CTAs, each CTA processes the entire dataset, multiplying total work by ~3263x. Also avoid when the while-loop condition references xnumel as a runtime value that Triton cannot bound at compile time — this prevents loop unrolling optimizations and may cause compiler pathologies.
framework_notes: In Triton, a persistent grid-stride loop REQUIRES the kernel_function launch grid to be reduced to the persistent CTA count (e.g., 1056). The stride hardcoded inside the kernel (1056 * XBLOCK) must exactly match the actual launched grid size * XBLOCK. If the diff shows the grid in kernel_function was not changed, the loop body executes grid_original / grid_persistent times more than intended.
